facts.raw_span: 45-year-old man
recent-onset dry cough
exertional dyspnea
no significant past medical history
12 cm mass in the anterior superior mediastinum
multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules suggestive of metastatic disease
neck edema, distended neck veins, and facial plethora
invasion of the superior vena cava above the azygos vein and thrombus extending into the left brachiocephalic trunk
multinodular proliferation of small, round, monomorphic cells with clear cytoplasm
diffuse strong WT1 positivity
moderate, patchy CD99 positivity
rapid symptomatic relief with heparin and high-dose corticosteroids

concepts.why: The patient's histopathology showing a multinodular proliferation of small, round, monomorphic cells with clear cytoplasm, along with diffuse strong WT1 positivity and moderate, patchy CD99 positivity, is consistent with Desmoplastic small round cell tumor.

The presence of a large mass in the anterior superior mediastinum and multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules suggestive of metastatic disease could be consistent with Thymoma, although the histopathological findings do not strongly support this diagnosis.

The location and size of the mediastinal mass, along with the presence of multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules, could suggest a Germ cell tumor, but the histopathological and immunohistochemical findings do not support this diagnosis.

The patient's presentation with a large mediastinal mass, multiple pulmonary nodules, and symptoms suggestive of superior vena cava syndrome could be consistent with Lymphoma, but the histopathological findings do not support this diagnosis.

The patient's histopathology showing a multinodular proliferation of small, round, monomorphic cells with clear cytoplasm, along with moderate, patchy CD99 positivity, could be consistent with Ewing's sarcoma, but the presence of diffuse strong WT1 positivity is more suggestive of Desmoplastic small round cell tumor.
